title: Batman appears at rain-soaked bus street
narration: The first time you see Batman, you think he has come to save you.

title: Batman takes radio and warns Alex
narration: Then he grabs your radio and says three words.  Don't open it.

title: Nia pounds fogged bus window
narration: Across the street, a little girl is trapped inside a school bus. The windows are fogging up. She's pounding on the glass. And the door is locked.

title: Wire on locked bus; Joker watches unseen
narration: Batman is telling you not to open it.  Because somewhere in Gotham, the Joker is watching. And the bus is part of his joke.

title: Six days earlier: rookie Alex
narration: Six days earlier, you were just a rookie cop who still believed a badge meant you could protect people.

title: Father locks shop; lamp in window
narration: Your name is Alex Reyes. You grew up in Gotham, in an apartment above your father's repair shop. Every night, your father locked the front door, checked it twice, and left a small lamp burning in the window.

title: Father explains lamp as marker of home
narration: You once asked him why he bothered. A lamp wasn't going to stop a criminal.  No, he said. But it tells you which window is home.

title: Graduation flashlight handoff
narration: The night you graduate from the academy, he gives you an old flashlight. The metal is scratched, the switch is loose, and the beam flickers when you shake it.

title: Alex laughs; father remains serious
narration: You laugh. He doesn't.  Keep it, he says. Just in case the lights go out.

title: Mara and Alex at reinforced precinct
narration: Your first partner is Officer Mara Bennett. She's been with the Gotham police long enough to remember when the station windows weren't reinforced.

title: Damaged bank and reporters
narration: On your first patrol, you pass the ruins of a bank. Half the front wall is gone. Reporters crowd behind a barricade, waiting for someone to say the Joker's name.

title: Mara approaches anxious bank employee
narration: Mara walks past them and stops beside a bank employee sitting on the curb. The woman keeps staring at her hands.  Her brother worked inside. No one has told her whether he made it out.

title: Mara gives Alex water bottle
narration: You want to chase the story. Mara hands you a bottle of water and asks you to stay with the woman while she finds out.

title: Mara returns with hospital news
narration: Twenty minutes later, Mara comes back. The woman's brother is alive. He was taken to a hospital across town.

title: Reporters film bank, ignore reunion
narration: There are no cameras when she tells her. The reporters are still pointing their lenses at the hole in the wall.

title: Bat-Signal illuminates clouds
narration: That night, you see the Bat-Signal for the first time. A great black shape against the clouds. For a moment, even the traffic seems to slow.

title: Mara drives while Alex looks up
narration: You look up. Mara keeps driving.  You ask if Batman will catch the Joker.  Maybe, she says. But even if he does, somebody still has to answer the phones.

title: Robber hangs from fire escape
narration: On your third night, a robbery turns into a chase through the Narrows. By the time you arrive, the robber is hanging upside down from a fire escape, wrapped in a cable. A stolen bag lies beneath him, untouched.

title: Cape disappears over roof
narration: You look up. A cape disappears over the edge of a roof.  Your first real glimpse of Batman lasts less than a second.

title: Paramedics and dangling robber
narration: The robber is yelling that the bat broke his arm. The paramedics say his arm is fine. His pride is a different story.  You almost smile. Mara doesn't.

title: Residents stare at rooftop
narration: She points to the people watching from their windows. They're not watching the robber. They're watching the roof.  In Gotham, she says, even the good news makes people afraid to look up.

title: Red-ribbon package at precinct
narration: On your fourth day, a package arrives at the station. No return address. A bright red ribbon around a plain white box.  The desk sergeant clears the room and calls the bomb squad.

title: Specialist releases wind-up toy
narration: Inside, they find a cheap wind-up toy. A little policeman with a painted smile.  Its key has been turned all the way. When the specialist releases it, the toy marches across the table, bumps into a wall, and falls over.

title: Message attached to toy
narration: Taped to its back is a message.  How many cops does it take to save Gotham?  Underneath, in red ink: Let's find out.

title: Toy sealed in evidence
narration: By evening, the toy is in evidence. Everyone at the station is pretending they aren't thinking about it.  Mara tells you to go home and sleep.

title: Alex calls father at repair shop
narration: You call your father instead. He says the shop lights have been flickering again. You promise to stop by after your shift and fix the loose switch.  Then the line goes dead.

title: Blackout moves across city
narration: On your sixth night, Gotham loses power.  Not all at once. First a few blocks. Then another. Traffic lights go black. Storefronts disappear. Far away, the Bat-Signal clicks off halfway through its sweep, leaving an empty circle in the clouds.

title: Dispatch calls over cruiser radio
narration: Calls flood the radio. A bridge is jammed. An alarm is ringing at a hospital. Somewhere near Robinson Park, people report a bus stopped in the middle of the street.  You and Mara are closest.

title: Nia alone inside bus
narration: When you arrive, the bus is empty except for one child. She's sitting in the back, wearing a yellow raincoat, holding a small flashlight against the window.

title: Shaking bus driver describes Joker
narration: The driver is outside, shaking. He says a man in a purple coat stopped the bus, sent everyone else away, and locked the girl inside.

title: Phone rings in driver pocket
narration: A telephone rings in the driver's pocket.  He says the man gave it to him. He was told to answer when a police officer arrived.

title: Mara calls specialists as Nia knocks
narration: You tell him not to touch it. Mara steps between him and the bus and calls for the bomb squad. The little girl sees your uniform and starts banging on the window.

title: Mara answers phone on speaker
narration: The phone keeps ringing.  Mara answers on speaker.  A man's voice asks whether the city is enjoying the dark. You know that voice, even though you have never heard it in person. Every cop in Gotham does.

title: Joker speaks through phone; wire detail
narration: The Joker says the bus door is connected to a device. Open it, and something goes off. He doesn't say what. He doesn't say where.  Then he laughs and hangs up.

title: Nia drops flashlight inside bus
narration: You look at the girl. She presses a hand against the glass. Her flashlight slips from her fingers and rolls beneath a seat.

title: Alex steps toward bus door
narration: The bomb squad is on its way, but the roads are blocked. The driver says the girl has been alone for nearly half an hour. The windows are getting harder to see through.  You take a step toward the door.

title: Batman lands and cape settles
narration: Something lands on the roof above you. A heavy shape. A cape settles against the brick.  Batman drops into the street.  For a second, nobody moves. The driver steps back. Even Mara looks up.

title: Batman takes radio, warns dispatch
narration: You start explaining, but Batman has already seen the wire near the door. He takes your radio.  Don't open it.  Then he tells dispatch what he's found. His voice is low, steady. He asks Mara to move everyone back. You expect him to open the bus himself.  He doesn't.

title: Batman scans surrounding rooftops
narration: He checks the street, the rooftops, the abandoned cars. The Joker wanted an audience. Batman wants to know where the audience is hiding.

title: Batman answers second call
narration: The phone rings again.  This time Batman answers.  The Joker sounds delighted. He says there are two problems tonight. A child on a bus, and a room full of patients at a hospital whose backup power is about to fail.  He tells Batman he can save one, but not both.

title: Batman asks hospital; call ends
narration: Batman asks which hospital.  The Joker laughs. Find out.  The call ends.

title: Mara receives hospital report
narration: Batman looks at Mara. She has already requested confirmation from dispatch. A moment later, the report comes back. One hospital has lost backup power, and emergency crews are responding. No one yet knows whether the Joker caused it.

title: Batman assesses bus and points to wire
narration: Batman looks at the child. Then at the far end of the street.  You think he's about to leave her.  He tells Mara the bomb squad is two blocks away. He points out the wire and asks her to relay everything he's seen.

title: Batman tells Alex to stay; grapples away
narration: Then he turns to you.  Stay with her.  That's it. No speech. No promise.  He fires a line into the darkness and disappears over the rooftops.

title: Alex watches roof; Nia at window
narration: You stare after him. The girl is still at the window.  The Joker wanted you to see this as a choice between two lives. Batman left a team at the bus and went where he might be needed next. You don't know whether it will be enough.

title: Nia cries; memory of shop lamp
narration: The girl starts crying. You can't hear her through the glass, but you can see her shoulders shaking.  You remember your father's shop. The little lamp in the window.

title: Alex signals Nia with old flashlight
narration: You pull out the old flashlight. The beam flickers. You tap the switch, point it toward the bus, and raise your free hand.  The girl sees you. She wipes her face and raises her hand too.

title: Specialists assess; Alex maintains signal
narration: You keep the light on her window. When it flickers, you tap it again.  Mara stands beside you, speaking to the arriving specialists. The bomb squad examines the wire while firefighters keep the street clear. Nobody asks you to be a hero. They ask you to stay where the girl can see you.  So you do.

title: Specialist signals safe; Nia reunited
narration: The specialist gives Mara a signal. The device has been made safe. A firefighter opens the door, and the girl climbs down into her mother's arms.  You hear her crying now. So is her mother.  The flashlight goes out in your hand.

title: Hospital power restored
narration: At the hospital, the emergency crew restores power.

title: Radio reports Joker in custody
narration: Later, the radio reports that Batman found the Joker nearby. There is no dramatic announcement, just officers requesting transport and a medic. The Joker is in custody. Tonight, at least.

title: Morning television debates Batman
narration: By morning, the city is arguing about Batman again. Some people say he should never have left the bus. Others say the hospital needed him more. On television, the reporters show the Joker's grin and the black sky where the Bat-Signal went dark.

title: Mother thanks team; no cameras
narration: Nobody shows the little girl waving through the window. Nobody mentions Mara or the specialists who opened the door. That's all right. Her mother knows their names.

title: Alex reaches father shop at dawn
narration: At the end of your shift, you go to your father's shop. The lights are back on, but the lamp in the window is dark.

title: Sleeping father; Alex repairs lamp
narration: Your father is asleep in his chair. You don't wake him. You set the old flashlight on the counter, open your toolbox, and fix the loose switch on the lamp.

title: Lamp glows; father wakes
narration: When it glows, your father opens one eye.  Long night? he asks.

title: Delivery worker and passing bus
narration: You look outside. Across the street, a delivery driver is unlocking a shop. A bus passes. Somewhere above the buildings, the clouds begin to turn gray.

title: Officers answer phones as city wakes
narration: The Joker will escape again someday. In Gotham, everyone knows that. Batman will be there when he does.  And someone will still have to answer the phones. Someone will have to stand beside the people waiting for news.

title: Father offers to repair flashlight
narration: Your father looks at the flashlight on the counter. The beam is dead.  I can fix it, he says.  You smile. I know.

title: Alex looks at waking city; end question
narration: If you were an ordinary cop in Gotham, would you stay? And which world should we enter next?
